issue.title: test_ace_page_group_rejects_overlapping_checkouts raises NoMatches on #stitches-timeline under a parallel CI leg
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-um.9.5.3 (note #3) during epic sase-um.9.5 ("Complete the
interrupted sase-um.9 release-gate landing"), routed to a task by sase-um.9.5.land on
2026-08-29. Recorded as a node-specific bead rather than a corroboration because
sase-ct, the retired umbrella for "flaky ACE TUI tests under the full parallel just test
run", forbids +1/reopen and routes exactly this shape of report to a narrow task named
for the failing node ID. No other open or closed task bead names this node.

The failure is an unhandled `textual.css.query.NoMatches` for `#stitches-timeline`, so
the node asserts against a widget that has not mounted yet rather than timing out on a
wait. That is the same family of readiness defect as the `#frontmatter-raw` NoMatches
tracked by sase-nf and sase-pe: an ACE page queries a child by ID on a path that assumes
mount has completed. Triage should look for the missing readiness wait (or the mount
ordering that makes the query legal) rather than adding a bare retry.

The parent epic plan (sase-um.9) already treated this node as a serial-pass flake in its
attribution, so this bead exists to make that disposition durable rather than to
re-argue it.

task_type_fields.evidence:
One CI failure, two passes on the same node:

- Full CI run 33167273442, test(3.13) leg: FAILED with
  textual.css.query.NoMatches: no nodes match '#stitches-timeline'.
- Full CI run 33216659649, test(3.13) leg (later SHA affc43a6f): the node passed.
- Serial rerun on master tip 1a1463028 in the epic's workspace: passed.

Fail/pass shape: red once under a parallel CI leg, green on the next CI run of the same
leg and green on an isolated serial rerun -- the class sase-ct was retired for. Not
reproduced locally under load; nobody has attempted a targeted parallel repro yet.
Do not mute.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: just test-scoped -- tests/test_ace_testing.py (red only under the full parallel/CI lane)
